title: CoT Faithfulness Failure Patterns by Step Position: Early vs. Late Reasoning
original_idea: Use the unlearning-reasoning-steps methodology to ablate individual CoT steps. Measure which step positions, when unlearned, most strongly affect answer quality. Characterize faithfulness failures by position.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Positional analysis of faithfulness failures guides where to focus monitoring. Practical for interpretability tool design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Unlearning reasoning steps requires fine-tuning and gradient-based methods. Advanced ML expertise needed. Not beginner-appropriate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Implementing the unlearning methodology, running ablations, and analyzing results. Technically complex and time-consuming. Exceeds 30hrs for beginners.

novelty.reasoning: This is directly addressed by existing work. 'Measuring Chain of Thought Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning Steps' (EMNLP 2025) segments reasoning chains and unlearns individual steps to measure faithfulness -- exactly the proposed methodology. FaithCoT-Bench (2025) includes 'Removing Steps' and 'Early Answering' as perturbation methods. The 'early answering from truncated CoT' metric directly measures positional importance. The idea's accessibility score of 1 already reflects this requires advanced ML expertise (fine-tuning, gradient-based methods), and the core research question is largely answered.
